report:
### Conclusion
The claim is **supported by strong scientific evidence**: higher olive oil intake is associated with a reduced risk of stroke.

### Summary of Evidence

1. **Randomized Clinical Trials:** The landmark PREDIMED trial provided high-level evidence that a Mediterranean diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil significantly reduced primary cardiovascular events, specifically demonstrating a marked reduction in stroke risk compared to a standard reduced-fat control diet ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29897866/), [ScienceDaily](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2013/02/130225181536.htm)).
2. **Meta-Analyses and Epidemiological Studies:** Comprehensive meta-analyses evaluating observational cohorts and intervention studies confirm an inverse relationship between higher olive oil consumption and the incidence of stroke and overall cardiovascular disease ([Cambridge Core](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-nutrition/article/olive-oil-consumption-and-risk-of-chd-andor-stroke-a-metaanalysis-of-casecontrol-cohort-and-intervention-studies/79A90337470271D8A8CE2FDC77BD869E), [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38568797/)).
3. **Biological Mechanisms:** Olive oil—particularly extra-virgin olive oil—is rich in monounsaturated fatty acids (oleic acid) and polyphenols. These compounds improve blood pressure control, enhance endothelial function, reduce systemic inflammation, and lower oxidative stress, all of which protect against cerebrovascular events.

In conclusion, both observational and clinical trial data confirm that regular olive oil consumption contributes to lower stroke risk.
